description: Assets, trust boundaries, entry points, threats mapped to mitigations, and the residual risk accepted, kept up to date with the system.
A point where data crosses from less trusted to more trusted (inbound content into the context, tool calls into internal APIs, output into a browser).
What remains after the mitigations, stated with the reason it is acceptable and how it is monitored.
Spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege: a classic prompt for threats at each boundary.
Every concern has an effective mitigation, and every mitigation exists in the configuration, so the document and the system cannot drift apart unnoticed.
Remove the capability, then narrow it, then gate it, then detect misuse. Each step down is weaker.
